To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cross modal self supervised learning is a promising approach for representation learning in both video and audio.

(1) cross modal clustering is more effective than single modal clustering for self supervised learning; (2) cross modal self supervised learning is more effective than fully supervised pretraining; and (3) cross modal self supervision is more effective for video than for audio.
cross modal deep clustering is a powerful method for self supervised learning.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: Can we learn video and audio representations in a self-supervised way by leveraging their strong correlation and their intrinsic differences?
the problem of learning video and audio representations from large scale unlabelled data.

the question of whether it is possible to learn video representations from audio alone and if so, whether such representations can be better than fully supervised learning of video representations from video alone.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

XDC achieves state-of-the-art results in self-supervised representation learning for video and audio modalities, outperforming other self-supervised methods, and even large scale fully supervised methods, on several video and audio benchmarks.
XDC outperform all other self supervised methods for video representation learning.

we propose a novel method that outperformed all the other state of the art approaches for self supervised learning and also outperformed supervised learning for action recognition on a large scale dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
XDC is a simple yet powerful self supervised learning framework for multi modal data.
XDC is the best self supervised method for video representation learning.
XDC is the best self supervised learning method for both video and audio modalities and it outperforms fully supervised pretraining on video data for action recognition.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self supervised learning can be improved by exploiting the differences between the modalities in addition to their correlation.
the combination of cross modal correlation and difference is a powerful supervisory signal for self supervised learning.
cross modal self supervision can lead to state of the art self supervised video representations that can even surpass supervised representations.
